titulo: Read the decision before you ask
subtitulo: Six sign pairs for doors, queues, toilets, hours and boundaries — recognition only
cena: A door is coming up fast, both hands full, and the only useful information about which way it swings is one word printed on a small metal plate.
frasePiso: Your eyes can resolve the next action before your mouth has to ask for help.

steps.pt: B10 is silent — no pronouncing, no copying. Just recognise a sign and move: enter, exit, pull, push, queue, toilets, time, stop.
At a divided doorway, choose the flow first — entrada in, salida out. Let the arrow and people confirm it, don't stop to translate.
On a manual door, jale pulls toward you, empuje pushes away. Read it before your hand reaches the handle.
Fila marks where waiting begins, taquilla is the ticket window. If a queue leads there, join the back, don't walk to the glass.
Both signs lead to the toilets — follow the pictogram and arrow. No sign? Fall back to B08's location question.
Horario shows the hours for that place specifically — check today's range. Cerrado ends it: change time or place.
Último acceso is the deadline to enter, not closing time. Solo personal is a boundary — stop, find the public route.

steps.promptPt: The sign said SALIDA and you need the other one. Speak now.
You read FILA and it is enormous. Ask if there is a second one. Speak now.
The sign said SOLO PERSONAL and you are not sure it applies to you. Speak now.
You saw the word but not the arrow. Speak now.

steps.pt: B10 complete. Entrance, exit, pull, push, queue, toilets, hours, last entry, staff only — sign to decision to body.

aprofundar.titulo: A sign is a compressed action

secoes.titulo: Transparent writing still needs a decision
secoes.corpo: An English speaker can recognise many letters and still choose the wrong action. B10 does not reward approximate translation; every surface is tied to one bodily or planning decision.
This SKU teaches JALE and EMPUJE for manual doors. It does not import the Spain-centred TIRAR pair. Read the surface that is actually present; automatic doors are outside the drill.
SANITARIOS and BAÑOS are recognition targets. The arrow and restroom pictogram carry equal weight, which makes the skill robust when only one word is visible.
HORARIO tells you to read today's line. The course freezes no opening time, midday closure or weekly rest day. ÚLTIMO ACCESO is a separate deadline and must not be treated as closing time.

permissao: You are allowed to get this wrong once and just watch what everyone else does next. B10 is receptive on purpose — there is no spoken test here, so a misread sign costs you a wrong turn, not an embarrassing sentence in front of a queue.
espelho: Every traveller has misjudged a push/pull door or missed a queue's actual starting point in their own country at least once — B10 isn't teaching a uniquely Mexican skill, it's making explicit a reading habit fluent locals do automatically and never think about.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You walk toward a glass ticket window to ask your question directly, and several people who were standing off to the side suddenly look at you.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: They're just staring, or this place has no real queue system.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The queue almost certainly starts at a FILA sign or a visible line of people you didn't register as a queue, and walking straight to the window reads as cutting in, not as a reasonable question for a stranger to ask.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Look for a FILA marker or the back of a visible line before approaching any staffed window directly.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You join the process everyone else is already following instead of becoming the visible exception to it.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not at a counter with clearly no queue at all — the rule is about respecting an existing line, not inventing one where none exists.
